title: Shadow variant escalation loop remediation and runbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Post-incident ticket to capture investigation, immediate mitigations, and durable fixes after a shadowed model-variant mismatch caused cross-region reroute amplification and request fanout loops during a capacity spike. Deliverables: incident RCA, short-term throttles/failovers, runbook updates, and telemetry/guardrail changes to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-27 14:03 UTC a subset of production traffic experienced escalating cross-region rerouting for ~37 minutes. Symptoms: doubling retries, increased tail latency, and upstream 503/422 errors. Root trigger: shadow routing tag mismatch + stale policy cache combined with aggressive retry/backoff settings, which caused the smart-routing orchestra to reassign requests to incompatible model variants and then re-fanout when compatibility checks failed.
timeline: 2026-02-27 13:58 UTC — First anomalous latency spike detected on per-route dashboard (route /v1/chat).
2026-02-27 14:03 UTC — Error rate and retry volume increased; automated alert for routing error budget fired.
2026-02-27 14:05 UTC — On-call SRE pinpoints repeated variant incompatibility errors (consumer-side 422) and early fallback loops.
2026-02-27 14:12 UTC — Emergency throttles applied: global retry cap lowered and shadow routing disabled for affected policy tiers.
2026-02-27 14:40 UTC — Traffic stabilized after cache flush and temporary conservative fallback policy.
2026-02-27 15:00 UTC — Post-incident bridge opened to capture action items and plan permanent mitigations.
root_cause: Policy state drift: a recent config push introduced a new 'shadow-variant' tag that was not added to the policy-compatibility matrix, so runtime compatibility checks returned false for shadowed variants.

Stale policy cache TTL: regional policy caches had a longer TTL than the control-plane push, so some regional routers continued to prefer old routing decisions while others took the new one, creating asymmetric routing.
Retry amplification: default retry/backoff logic did not differentiate between deterministic incompatibility errors and transient capacity errors, causing immediate retries that amplified fanout.
No circuit-breaker for repeated 4xx variant incompatibility errors — the system treated them like soft failures rather than hard mismatches.
immediate_mitigation: Disabled shadow routing for the affected policy group (hotfix via control-plane rollback).
Flushed regional policy caches across all regions to re-hydrate with authoritative state (scripted: infra/scripts/flush_policy_cache.sh).
Applied temporary retry policy: set max_retries=1 and added exponential jitter for 10 minutes on affected routes.
Deployed an interim compatibility-check short-circuit to treat deterministic incompatibility (variant mismatch) as non-retriable and trigger immediate fallback to pinned-compatible variant.
long_term_fixes: Policy compatibility matrix validation: add preflight CI gate to ensure every new variant tag is present in compatibility maps before control-plane rollout.
TTL alignment: make regional policy caches TTL selectable per rollout and default to immediate invalidation for config pushes that touch routing logic.
Circuit-breaker enhancement: classify 4xx incompatibility responses as hard failures and install per-variant circuit-breakers with cooldown windows.
Retry logic rewrite: add error-class-aware retry strategy (no retries for deterministic incompatibilities; graduated backoff for transient server errors).
Routing telemetry: add metrics for variant-mismatch-rate, shadowed-requests-count, and per-policy-fanout-ratio to detect early amplification patterns.
Runbook and playbook: create a dedicated 'shadow routing escalation' playbook with step-by-step rollback, cache-flush commands, and measurement checks.

acceptance_criteria: CI preflight rejects control-plane pushes that reference unknown variant tags in runtime-config repo (green build for config changes only).
Circuit-breaker triggers on variant-mismatch errors in canary and staging and prevents fanout amplification for >95% of synthetic mismatch cases.
Regional policy cache invalidation occurs within 30s of a config push affecting routing or rejects the push until invalidation can be guaranteed.
Monitoring alerts fire when per-route amplification ratio exceeds 1.5x or variant-mismatch-rate > 0.1% for 5 minutes.
